text:
alex.k: quick check — proposing a tiny canary for the new ephemeral-probe sampling + routing tag. want to route 2% of write requests to the probe path that keeps a pseudonymized request blob for 3h.
maria_g: 2% SGTM for canary, what's the exact data kept? only headers + anonymized body?
kevin_h: plan was: keep request metadata (route, model, latency, user_tier) + pseudonymized body hash, and a minimal response code + token_count. no raw user text.
sophiep: +1 but we need to be explicit about the hashing: are we double-salting per-tenant? wondering about correlation attacks.
alex.k: yep — per-tenant HMAC with tenant-specific key from KMS, then a global rotation salt. storage only stores first 12 chars of base64(hmac) to keep size down.
kevin_h: sample config snippet: 
```yaml
probe_sampling:
  rate: 0.02
  store_ttl: 10800 # seconds (3h)
  pseudonymize: hmac-sha256
  truncate: 12
  tenant_key: kms://projects/payments/key1
```
maria_g: looks good. question: how will this show up in the console? Product wants a per-route probe count + pct-sampled metric. also an alert if redaction failures > 0.1% over 10m.
sophiep: console dashboard should show: sampled_rate, probe_errors, redaction_failures, sampling_bias (compare sampled distribution vs traffic). Also a drilldown: example pseudonym hashes (no raw text) and timestamps.
kevin_h: note on quotas — sampled probes currently count against customer request quotas. do we want that? It inflates usage metrics.
alex.k: proposal: don't charge customers for probe copies (internal-only), but still account for them in system capacity calculations. that means meter doesn't increment. ops-team ok with that?
ops-oncall: needs ops approval. exempting meter could mask abuse. can we gate it behind a billing_exempt flag only for internal-telemetry tenants?
maria_g: product ok with billing_exempt for telemetry-only probes. but we need a clear audit trail that shows how many exemptions were applied.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/ephemeral-probe @ 6:15pm UTC. running preflight checks.
sophiep: rollout plan: stage 1: 0.02 rate internal tenants only. stage 2: 0.02 across small external beta tenants (5) with legal signoff. monitor redaction_failures, pseudonym_collision (should be 0), and end-to-end latency impact.
kevin_h: question about redaction edgecases — if pseudonymization fails, what do we store? we should store an error tag, no content. and increment redaction_failures metric.
alex.k: agreed. code will fallback to no-store + emit metric + sample id for trace.
maria_g: UX: add a console toggle to view probe payloads for 3h (read-only, requires inspect role). should also show when the tenant_key was used (kms key id).
ops-oncall: reminder: ensure KMS access auditing is on for probe keys. otherwise legal will flag it.
sophiep: final ask — add a routing policy: if runtime load > 85% across a region, route probes to a low-priority background queue (no quota, delayed by up to 30s). want to surface that in the dashboard.
kevin_h: I can add the routing logic in router service. quick pseudocode: 
```py
if region_load > 0.85:
  route = 'probe-background'
else:
  route = 'probe-normal'
```
alex.k: ok if we merge this today I'd like a post-deploy sync in #eng-oncall in 1h to validate metrics. any objections?
maria_g: none from product. +:thumbsup:
ops-oncall: will join.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: feature/ephemeral-probe @ 6:42pm UTC.
kevin_h: post-deploy checks: emitting metrics now. sample_rate.reported=0.02, redaction.failures=0, probe.queue=normal.
sophiep: seeing one redaction failure in europe-west-1 — investigating.
maria_g: thanks — keep thread updated. we should capture lessons for the rollout doc.
